summary: A thief pays double for anything he steals. If he steals an ox or a sheep and then shechts or sells it, he pays four or five times. Someone who steals from a thief does not pay these extra amounts.

chunks.en: The rule of paying double covers more
chunks.st: The principle of double payment applies

chunks.en: than the rule of paying four and five times,
chunks.st: more broadly than the principle of fourfold or fivefold payment,

chunks.he: שֶׁמִּדַּת תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל נוֹהֶגֶת בֵּין בְּדָבָר
chunks.en: because the rule of double works both for something
chunks.st: as the principle of double payment applies both to the theft of

chunks.he: שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים וּבֵין בְּדָבָר
chunks.en: that is alive and for something
chunks.st: something that is alive and to the theft of

chunks.en: that is not alive,
chunks.st: something that is not alive,

chunks.en: but the rule of four and five does not
chunks.st: but the principle of fourfold or fivefold payment

chunks.en: work except for an ox or a sheep only,
chunks.st: applies only to the theft of an ox or a sheep,

chunks.en: as it says, "If
chunks.st: as it is stated: “If

chunks.en: a man steals an ox or a sheep and shechts it
chunks.st: a man steal an ox or a sheep, and slaughter it

chunks.en: or sells it..."
chunks.explain: Then he pays five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.
chunks.st: or sell it, he shall pay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep” (Exodus 21:37).
chunks.stMore: Having stated a limitation to the halakha of fourfold and fivefold payment, the mishna mentions a further limitation, which applies to all three types of payments.

chunks.en: Someone who steals from a thief
chunks.st: One who steals an item after a thief has already stolen it, i.e., one who steals a stolen item,

chunks.en: does not pay double,
chunks.st: does not pay the double payment to the thief or to the prior owner,

chunks.en: and someone who shechts or sells after
chunks.st: nor does one who slaughters or sells an ox or a sheep

chunks.en: the thief does not pay four or five times.
chunks.st: after a thief has already stolen it pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.
chunks.stMore: Rather, he pays only the principal, i.e., the value of the item he stole.

summary: Cases where a thief who stole an animal and then shechted or sold it still pays four or five times, even if he did it in a sinful way. Rabbi Shimon disagrees about two cases.

chunks.en: If he stole, as two witnesses said,
chunks.st: The mishna lists a series of cases in which a thief is required to pay the fourfold or fivefold penalty. If one stole an animal, as established based on the testimony of two witnesses,

chunks.en: and shechted or sold it, as they said, or
chunks.st: and he subsequently slaughtered the animal or sold it, also based on the testimony of the same witnesses,

chunks.en: as two other witnesses said,
chunks.st: or based on the testimony of two other witnesses,

chunks.en: he pays four or five times.
chunks.st: he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

chunks.en: If he stole it and sold it on Shabbos,
chunks.st: If one stole an animal and sold it on Shabbat,

chunks.en: stole it and sold it for avodah zarah,
chunks.st: or if he stole it and sold it for idol worship,

chunks.en: stole it and shechted it on Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: or if he stole it and slaughtered it on Yom Kippur, he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
chunks.stMore: Although his sale or slaughter in these circumstances involved a sin, he is not liable to receive the death penalty for the sale and must consequently pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.

chunks.en: stole from his father's animals and shechted or sold it,
chunks.st: If one stole an animal of his father’s and then slaughtered it or sold it,

chunks.en: and after that his father died,
chunks.st: and afterward his father died and he inherited his father’s estate either on his own or in partnership with his brothers,

chunks.en: stole and shechted it and after that made it hekdesh:
chunks.st: or if he stole an animal and slaughtered it and afterward he consecrated it,

chunks.en: he pays four or five times.
chunks.st: he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

chunks.en: If he stole and shechted it for medicine or for dogs,
chunks.st: In the case of one who stole an animal and slaughtered it, not for the purpose of eating its meat, but to use it for medicinal purposes or to feed the meat to dogs,

chunks.en: or one who shechts and it turns out to be treifah,
chunks.st: and likewise a thief who slaughters the animal to eat its meat but it was found to be an animal with a condition that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa],

words.note: An animal with a sickness or injury that makes it not kosher.

chunks.en: or one who shechts a regular animal in the Azarah,
chunks.explain: The Azarah is the courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: or a thief who slaughters a non-sacred animal in the Temple courtyard,

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: he pays four or five times.
chunks.st: he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says he does not pay in these two cases.
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon exempts the thief from the fourfold or fivefold payment in these last two cases,
chunks.stMore: as he maintains that the legal status of an act of slaughter that is not fit for accomplishing its full ritual purpose is not considered an act of slaughter.

summary: If witnesses who said a person stole and shechted are found to be eidim zomemin (lying witnesses), they must pay what they tried to make him pay.

chunks.en: He stole, as two witnesses said,
chunks.st: If one stole an ox or a sheep, as established based on the testimony of two witnesses,

chunks.en: and shechted or sold it, as they said,
chunks.st: and he subsequently slaughtered the animal or sold it, also based on the testimony of the same witnesses,

chunks.en: and they turned out to be eidim zomemin:
chunks.explain: Witnesses proven to be lying, because they were somewhere else.
chunks.st: and these witnesses were found to be conspiring witnesses,

words.note: Lying witnesses, shown to have been somewhere else at the time.

chunks.en: they pay everything.
chunks.st: these witnesses pay everything, i.e., not only the principal amount but also the fourfold or fivefold payment.
chunks.stMore: This is in accordance with the Torah’s decree with regard to conspiring witnesses: “You shall do to him as he had conspired to do to his brother” (Deuteronomy 19:19). Since these witnesses attempted to obligate the alleged thief to pay the fourfold or fivefold payment, they themselves must pay that full amount.

chunks.en: He stole, as two witnesses said, and shechted
chunks.st: With regard to one who stole an ox or a sheep, as established based on the testimony of two witnesses, and he subsequently slaughtered the animal

chunks.en: or sold it, as two other witnesses said,
chunks.st: or sold it, based on the testimony of two other witnesses,

chunks.en: and both groups turned out to be zomemin:
chunks.st: if both these witnesses and those witnesses were found to be conspiring witnesses,

chunks.en: the first ones pay double,
chunks.st: the first set of witnesses, who testified about the theft of the animal, pay the alleged thief the double payment, which is what they had conspired to cause him to pay.

chunks.en: and the last ones pay three times.
chunks.explain: Three is what is left over above the double.
chunks.st: And the last set of witnesses, who attested to the slaughter or sale of the animal, pay the alleged thief a twofold payment for a sheep or a threefold payment for an ox, which they had conspired to cause him to pay over and above the double payment.

chunks.en: If only the last ones turned out to be zomemin,
chunks.st: If only the witnesses in the last set were found to be conspiring witnesses, while the testimony about the theft remains intact,

chunks.en: he pays double,
chunks.st: the thief pays the double payment to the animal’s owner

chunks.en: and they pay three times.
chunks.st: and the second set of witnesses pay the alleged thief the twofold or threefold payment, the amount over and above the double payment, which is what they had conspired to cause him to pay.

chunks.en: If one of the last ones is a zomem,
chunks.st: If only one individual from the last set of witnesses was found to be a conspiring witness,

chunks.en: the second testimony is cancelled.
chunks.st: the second testimony is nullified, as it was not submitted by two valid witnesses, whereas the first testimony remains intact.

chunks.en: If one of the first ones is a zomem,
chunks.st: If one individual from the first set of witnesses is found to be a conspiring witness,

chunks.en: the whole testimony is cancelled,
chunks.st: the entire testimony concerning the thief is nullified.

chunks.en: because if there was no stealing, there is no
chunks.st: The reason is that if there is no theft established by reliable testimony there is no liability for

chunks.en: shechting and no selling.
chunks.st: slaughtering the animal and there is no liability for selling it.

summary: Cases where a thief pays only double, not four or five times: when there was only one witness for the shechting, or when the shechting or selling was not really his to pay for. Rabbi Shimon adds a rule about korbanos.

chunks.en: He stole, as two witnesses said,
chunks.st: If one stole an ox or a sheep, as established based on the testimony of two witnesses,

chunks.he: וְטָבַח וּמָכַר עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד,
chunks.en: and shechted or sold it, as one witness said,
chunks.st: and he subsequently slaughtered or sold the stolen animal, as established based on the testimony of one witness

chunks.en: or as he said himself:
chunks.st: or based on his own admission, i.e., he himself admitted that he performed these acts, without there being any witness testimony,

chunks.en: he pays double,
chunks.st: he pays the double payment,

chunks.en: but he does not pay four or five times.
chunks.st: but he does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.

chunks.en: If he stole and shechted it on Shabbos,
chunks.st: If one stole an animal and slaughtered it on Shabbat, which is a capital offense,

chunks.en: stole and shechted it for avodah zarah,
chunks.st: or if he stole an animal and slaughtered it for the purpose of idol worship,

chunks.en: stole from his father's animals,
chunks.st: or if he stole his father’s animal

chunks.en: and his father died,
chunks.st: and subsequently his father died,

chunks.en: and after that he shechted or sold it,
chunks.st: and afterward he slaughtered or sold it,

chunks.he: גָּנַב וְהִקְדִּישׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ טָבַח וּמָכַר,
chunks.en: stole and made it hekdesh and after that shechted or sold it:
chunks.st: or if he stole an animal and subsequently he consecrated it as an offering and afterward he slaughtered or sold it,

chunks.en: he pays double, and he does not
chunks.st: in all these cases the thief pays the double payment,

chunks.en: pay four or five times.
chunks.st: but he does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: korbanos that the owner must replace if lost:
chunks.st: In the case of sacrificial animals for which the owner bears financial responsibility to replace with another animal if one of the original animals that one stole is lost or dies,

chunks.en: he pays four or five times.
chunks.st: the thief is obligated to pay the fourfold or fivefold payment if he slaughters one of the animals.

chunks.en: If the owner does not need to replace them, he does not pay.
chunks.st: If it is a sacrificial animal for which the owner bears no financial responsibility, the thief is exempt from the fourfold or fivefold payment.

summary: More cases where the thief pays only double: if he did not sell the whole animal, or the shechitah was not kosher. Stealing only counts once the animal leaves the owner's property.

chunks.en: If he sold it except for one hundredth of it,
chunks.st: If a thief sold a stolen animal in a partial fashion, e.g., except for one one-hundredth of it, which he kept for himself;

chunks.en: or he was a partner in it,
chunks.st: or if he had a partnership in owning the animal before stealing it;

chunks.en: or one who shechted and it became neveilah in his hand,
chunks.explain: Neveilah: an animal that is not kosher because it was not shechted right.
chunks.st: or in the case of a thief who slaughtered the stolen animal and it became non-kosher meat in his hand because he slaughtered it improperly;

words.note: Not kosher, because the shechitah was not done right.

chunks.en: or one who killed it in a way that is not shechitah,
chunks.st: or in the case of a thief who ripped open the animal rather than slaughtering it halakhically; or in the case of a thief who tore loose the gullet or windpipe of the animal as he slaughtered it, rendering the slaughter invalid,

words.en: and the one who tears out

chunks.en: he pays double, and he does not
chunks.st: in all these cases he pays the double payment

chunks.en: pay four or five times.
chunks.st: but does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.
chunks.stMore: The fourfold or five-fold payment applies only if the animal is entirely sold or if it is slaughtered in accordance with the halakhic definition of animal slaughter.

chunks.en: If he stole it on the owner's property, and shechted
chunks.st: If one stole an animal in its owner’s domain, i.e., he took hold of it or established control over it but had not yet removed it from the owner’s premises, and then he slaughtered it

chunks.en: or sold it outside their property,
chunks.st: or sold it outside of the owner’s domain;

chunks.en: or he stole it outside their property
chunks.st: or if he stole an animal outside of the owner’s domain

chunks.en: and shechted or sold it on their property,
chunks.st: and slaughtered it or sold it in the owner’s domain;

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁגָּנַב וְטָבַח וּמָכַר חוּץ מֵרְשׁוּתָם,
chunks.en: or he stole, shechted and sold it, all outside their property:
chunks.st: or if he stole an animal and slaughtered it or sold it, and all of this occurred outside the owner’s domain,

chunks.en: he pays four or five times.
chunks.st: in all of these cases, he must pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.

chunks.he: אֲבָל גָּנַב וְטָבַח וּמָכַר בִּרְשׁוּתָם, פָּטוּר:
chunks.en: But if he stole, shechted and sold it all on their property, he does not pay.
chunks.st: But if he stole it and slaughtered or sold it, and all of this occurred in the owner’s domain, he is exempt from any of the fines for theft,
chunks.stMore: as it is not considered theft until the stolen object is actually removed from the owner’s premises.

summary: A thief is only responsible once he lifts the animal or takes it out of the owner's property. The same is true if he gave it to someone else who did this for him.

chunks.en: If he was pulling it to go out,
chunks.st: If the thief was in the process of leading the animal and leaving the owner’s premises,

chunks.en: and it died on the owner's property,
chunks.st: and it died while it was still in the owner’s domain,

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. הִגְבִּיהוֹ אוֹ שֶׁהוֹצִיאוֹ מֵרְשׁוּת הַבְּעָלִים,
chunks.en: he does not pay. If he lifted it or took it out of the owner's property,
chunks.st: the thief is exempt from payment. If he lifted it up or led it out of the owner’s domain

chunks.en: and it died, he must pay.
chunks.st: and then the animal died, he is liable for his theft.
chunks.stMore: For an act to be considered theft, the thief must acquire the item by pulling it or moving it, which are ineffective forms of acquisition on the owner’s premises; or by lifting it up, which is effective even when performed in the owner’s domain.

chunks.he: נְתָנוֹ לִבְכוֹרוֹת בְּנוֹ אוֹ לְבַעַל חוֹבוֹ,
chunks.en: If he gave it to redeem his firstborn son, or to someone he owed,
chunks.st: If the thief gave the animal as payment for the redemption of his firstborn son, or as payment to a creditor,

chunks.en: to a watchman who is not paid,
chunks.st: or conveyed it for safeguarding to an unpaid bailee,

chunks.en: or to a borrower, to a paid watchman,
chunks.st: or lent it to a borrower, or conveyed it for safeguarding to a paid bailee,

chunks.en: or to a renter, and he was pulling it,
chunks.st: or leased it to a renter, and he was leading out the animal

chunks.en: and it died on the owner's property,
chunks.st: and it died in the owner’s domain,

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. הִגְבִּיהוֹ אוֹ שֶׁהוֹצִיאוֹ מֵרְשׁוּת הַבְּעָלִים,
chunks.en: he does not pay. If he lifted it or took it out of the owner's property,
chunks.st: the thief is exempt from payment. If that individual, following the thief’s instructions, lifted up the animal or led it out of the owner’s domain,

chunks.en: and it died, he must pay.
chunks.st: and it subsequently died, the thief is liable for the theft.
chunks.stMore: The thief is liable for instructing another to remove the animal for the purposes of payment of a debt, safekeeping, borrowing, or rental, as this is tantamount to the thief taking it with his own hands.

summary: Rules to keep animals from causing harm: where sheep, goats and chickens may not be raised, that pigs may not be raised, that dogs must be chained, and that traps for pigeons must be far from towns.

chunks.he: אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: We may not raise sheep and goats in Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: One may not raise small domesticated animals, i.e., sheep and goats, in settled areas of Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.stMore: as they graze on people’s crops.

chunks.en: but we may raise them in Surya,
chunks.st: But one may raise them in Syria,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that with regard to many other halakhot Syria is treated like Eretz Yisrael,

words.note: Syria, a land north of Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: and in the deserts of Eretz Yisrael.
chunks.st: and in the wilderness of Eretz Yisrael.

words.en: that are in the land of

chunks.en: We may not raise chickens in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: One may not raise chickens in Jerusalem,

chunks.en: because of the korbanos,
chunks.st: due to the sacrificial meat that is common there.
chunks.stMore: There is a concern that chickens will pick up garbage that imparts ritual impurity and bring it into contact with sacrificial meat, thereby rendering it ritually impure.

chunks.en: and Kohanim may not raise them in Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: And priests may not raise chickens anywhere in Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: because of their pure foods.
chunks.explain: Like terumah, which must stay tahor.
chunks.st: because of the many foods in a priest’s possession that must be kept ritually pure, e.g., teruma.

chunks.en: We may not raise pigs anywhere.
chunks.st: Furthermore, one may not raise pigs anywhere,

chunks.en: A person may not raise a dog,
chunks.st: and a person may not raise a dog

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה קָשׁוּר בְּשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת.
chunks.en: unless it is tied with a chain.
chunks.st: unless it is tied with chains.

chunks.en: We may not spread traps for pigeons,
chunks.st: One may spread out traps [nishovim] for pigeons

chunks.en: unless it is far
chunks.st: only if this was performed

chunks.en: from a town thirty ris.
chunks.explain: A ris is a measure of distance.
chunks.st: at a distance of at least thirty ris, which is 8,000 cubits, from any settled area,
chunks.stMore: to ensure that privately owned pigeons are not caught in the traps.
